49:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Hujurat In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful These are verses of the etiquette of God Almighty to His believing servants, regarding how they should treat the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with reverence, respect, veneration and glorification. God the Blessed and Exalted said: O you who have believed, do not precede God and His Messenger, meaning do not rush into things before him, but rather follow him in all matters. This is so that the general etiquette of Islamic etiquette includes the hadith of Mu’adh may God be pleased with him when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent him to Yemen: By what do you judge? He said: By the Book of God. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And if you do not find it? He said: “By the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “And if you do not find it?” He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I will exert my own judgment. He struck himself on the chest and said: “Praise be to God who guided the Messenger of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to that which pleases the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).” It was narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. The purpose of this is that he postponed his opinion, view and effort until after the Book and the Sunnah. If he had presented it before searching for them, it would have been a case of presenting it before God and His Messenger. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: Do not precede God and His Messenger means do not say anything that contradicts the Book and the Sunnah. Al-Awfi said on his authority: He forbade speaking before His words. Mujahid said: Do not fabricate anything against the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) until God Almighty decrees it through his tongue. Ad-Dahhak said: Do not decide a matter of your religious laws without God and His Messenger. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: Do not precede God and His Messenger with words or deeds. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Do not precede God and His Messenger meaning do not pray before the Imam. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that some people used to say, If only such and such had been revealed about such and such, if only such and such had been done, but God Almighty disliked that and He advanced in it: And fear God meaning in what He has commanded you. Indeed, God is Hearing meaning of your words. Knowing of your intentions. And the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet. This is a second etiquette with which God Almighty taught the believers not to raise their voices in front of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, above his voice. It has been narrated that it was revealed regarding the two sheikhs, Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. Al-Bukhari said: Busrah ibn Safwan Al-Lakhmi narrated to us, Nafi` ibn `Umar narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Mulaykah, who said: The two good men, Abu Bakr and `Umar may God be pleased with them, almost perished. They raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when the caravan of Banu Tamim came to him. One of them pointed to Al-Aqra` ibn Habis may God be pleased with him, the brother of Banu Majashi`, and the other pointed to another man. Nafi` said: I do not remember his name. Abu Bakr said to `Umar may God be pleased with them both, You only wanted to contradict me. He said: I did not want to contradict you. They raised their voices about that, so God revealed: “O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or be loud to him in speech like the loudness of some of you to others, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not.” Ibn Al-Zubayr may God be pleased with them both said: After this verse, `Umar may God be pleased with him did not hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) without asking him questions. He did not mention that from his father, meaning Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him. This was narrated only by him, not by Muslim. Then Al-Bukhari said: Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abi Malikah told me that Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, told him that a group of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: The matter of Al-Qa’qa’ bin Ma’bad, and Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Rather, the matter of Al-Aqra’ bin Habis, so Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: You only wanted to contradict me, so Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I did not want to contradict you, so they argued until their voices rose, and then the following verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger until the verse was completed, And if they had been patient until you came out to them… And thus he narrated it here alone as well. And Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Al-Fadl bin Sahl told us, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, Husayn bin Umar told us, on the authority of Mukhariq, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed, O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, I said: O Messenger of God, by God I will not speak to you except as a confidential brother. Husayn bin Umar, even though this is weak, we have narrated it from the hadith of Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf and Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with them in a similar manner, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Azhar bin Saad told us, Ibn Awn told us, Musa bin Anas told me, on the authority of Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) missed Thabit bin Qais may God be pleased with him, so a man said: O Messenger of God, I know what you know. So he went to him and found him in his house with his head bowed. So he said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: Evil was raising his voice above the voice of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. His deeds have been nullified and he is one of the people of Hellfire. So the man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him that he had said such and such. Moses said: So he returned to him a second time with great glad tidings and said: Go to him and tell him that you are not one of the people of Hellfire but one of the people of Paradise. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted this from this source. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim told us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet until His saying while you perceive not, Thabit ibn Qays ibn al-Shammas had a loud voice, so he said: I am the one who used to raise my voice to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I am one of the people of Hell. My deeds have been in vain, and he sat with his family, sad, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, missed him. Some of the people went to him and said to him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, missed you. What is wrong with you? He said: I am the one who raises my voice above the voice of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I say to him loudly: My deeds have been in vain. I am one of the people of Hell. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what he had said. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, rather he is one of the people of Paradise. Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: We used to see him walking among us and we knew that he was one of the people of Paradise. Then, on the day of Yamamah, we were somewhat dismayed, so Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas came, and he had embalmed himself and put on his shroud. He said: How evil is what you do to your peers. So he fought them until he was killed, may God be pleased with him. Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Bunani, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet to the end of the verse, Thabit, may God be pleased with him, sat in his house and said: I am one of the people of Hellfire, and he was kept away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Sa`d ibn Mu`adh: O Abu `Amr, what is the matter with Thabit that he is complaining? Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, said: He is my neighbor and I do not know of any complaint from him.” He said: Saad may God be pleased with him came to him and mentioned to him the statement of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Thabit may God be pleased with him said: This verse was revealed, and you know that I am the one among you who raises my voice to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so I am one of the people of Hellfire. Saad may God be pleased with him mentioned that to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rather, he is one of the people of Paradise. Then Muslim narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sa’id al-Darami on the authority of Hayyan ibn Hilal on the authority of Sulayman ibn al-Mughira with this chain of transmission, and he said that Saad ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him was not mentioned. It was also narrated on the authority of Qatan ibn Bashir on the authority of Ja’far ibn Sulayman on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him in a similar manner, and he said that it does not mention Saad ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him. He said: Asim bin Adi, may God be pleased with him, went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Weeping overcame him, so he went to his wife, Jamila, daughter of Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and said to her: When you enter my horse’s house, tie a nail to the rein. So she hit him with a nail until he came out, and he turned away and said: I will not come out until God, the Most High, takes me, or the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased with me. He said: Asim, may God be pleased with him, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him his story. He said: Go and call him to me. So Asim, may God be pleased with him, came to the place but did not find him, so he came to his family and found him in the horse’s house. He said to him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is calling you. He said: Break the rein. He said: So they went out and came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What makes you cry, Thabit? This story was also mentioned by more than one of the Successors, as God the Almighty forbade raising voices in the presence of the Messenger of God. We have narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the voices of two men in the Prophet’s Mosque, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and their voices had been raised. Scholars said: It is disliked to raise one’s voice at his grave, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as it was disliked during his life, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is respected alive and is always in his grave, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He forbade speaking loudly to him as a man speaks loudly to someone other than him, rather one should speak with calmness, dignity and respect. For this reason, God Almighty said: And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, just as God Almighty said: And do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of one of you to another. And the Almighty said: lest your deeds be rendered worthless while you perceive not. That is, We have only forbidden you from raising your voice in His presence, for fear that He might become angry at that and thus anger God, the Most High, because of His anger, and thus the deeds of the one who angered Him would be rendered worthless without him knowing, as it came in the Sahih: “A man may speak a word that pleases God, the Most High, without paying attention to it, and Paradise is written for him because of it. And a man may speak a word that angers God, the Most High, without paying attention to it, and because of it he falls into the Fire, the furthest distance between the heavens and the earth.” Then God, the Most High, urged people to lower their voices in His presence and urged them to do so, guided them to it, and encouraged them by saying: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God - those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety, that is, He has made them sincere for it and made them worthy and worthy of it. For them is forgiveness and a great reward. Imam Ahmad said in the Book of Asceticism: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He wrote to Umar: O Commander of the Faithful, is a man who does not desire sin and does not commit it better, or a man who desires sin. And he does not act upon it, so Omar, may God be pleased with him, wrote: Those who desire sin but do not act upon it, Those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety - for them is forgiveness and a great reward.

Scholars said: It is disliked to raise one’s voice at his grave, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as it was disliked during his life, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is respected alive and is always in his grave, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He forbade speaking loudly to him as a man speaks loudly to someone other than him, rather one should speak with calmness, dignity and respect. For this reason, God Almighty said: And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, just as God Almighty said: And do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of one of you to another. And the Almighty said: lest your deeds be rendered worthless while you perceive not. That is, We have only forbidden you from raising your voice in His presence, for fear that He might become angry at that and thus anger God, the Most High, because of His anger, and thus the deeds of the one who angered Him would be rendered worthless without him knowing, as it came in the Sahih: “A man may speak a word that pleases God, the Most High, without paying attention to it, and Paradise is written for him because of it. And a man may speak a word that angers God, the Most High, without paying attention to it, and because of it he falls into the Fire, the furthest distance between the heavens and the earth.” Then God, the Most High, urged people to lower their voices in His presence and urged them to do so, guided them to it, and encouraged them by saying: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God - those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety, that is, He has made them sincere for it and made them worthy and worthy of it. For them is forgiveness and a great reward. Imam Ahmad said in the Book of Asceticism: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He wrote to Umar: O Commander of the Faithful, is a man who does not desire sin and does not commit it better, or a man who desires sin. And he does not act upon it, so Omar, may God be pleased with him, wrote: Those who desire sin but do not act upon it, Those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety - for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
49:3: These are verses with which God the Almighty teaches His believing servants how to treat the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, with reverence, respect, veneration, and glorification. God the Blessed and Exalted said: O you who have believed, do not precede God and His Messenger, meaning do not rush into things before him, but rather follow him in all matters, so that the generality of this Islamic etiquette includes the hadith of Mu’adh, may God be pleased with him, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Yemen: By what do you judge? He said: By the Book of God the Almighty. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And if you do not find it? He said: “By the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And if you do not find it? He, may God be pleased with him, said: I will exert my own judgment. He struck himself on the chest and said: “Praise be to God who guided the Messenger of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to that which pleases the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” It was narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. The purpose of this is that he postponed his opinion, view and effort until after the Book and the Sunnah. If he had presented it before searching for them, it would have been a case of presenting it before God and His Messenger. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: Do not precede God and His Messenger means do not say anything that contradicts the Book and the Sunnah. Al-Awfi said on his authority: He forbade speaking before His words. Mujahid said: Do not fabricate anything against the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) until God Almighty decrees it through his tongue. Ad-Dahhak said: Do not decide a matter of your religious laws without God and His Messenger. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: Do not precede God and His Messenger with words or deeds. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Do not precede God and His Messenger meaning do not pray before the Imam. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that some people used to say, If only such and such had been revealed about such and such, if only such and such had been done, but God Almighty disliked that and He advanced in it: And fear God meaning in what He has commanded you. Indeed, God is Hearing meaning of your words. Knowing of your intentions. And the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet. This is a second etiquette with which God Almighty taught the believers not to raise their voices in front of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, above his voice. It has been narrated that it was revealed regarding the two sheikhs, Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. Al-Bukhari said: Busrah ibn Safwan Al-Lakhmi narrated to us, Nafi` ibn `Umar narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Mulaykah, who said: The two good men, Abu Bakr and `Umar may God be pleased with them, almost perished. They raised their voices in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when the caravan of Banu Tamim came to him. One of them pointed to Al-Aqra` ibn Habis may God be pleased with him, the brother of Banu Majashi`, and the other pointed to another man. Nafi` said: I do not remember his name. Abu Bakr said to `Umar may God be pleased with them both, You only wanted to contradict me. He said: I did not want to contradict you. They raised their voices about that, so God revealed: “O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or be loud to him in speech like the loudness of some of you to others, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not.” Ibn Al-Zubayr may God be pleased with them both said: After this verse, `Umar may God be pleased with him did not hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) without asking him questions. He did not mention that from his father, meaning Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him. This was narrated only by him, not by Muslim. Then Al-Bukhari said: Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abi Malikah told me that Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, told him that a group of Banu Tamim came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: The matter of Al-Qa’qa’ bin Ma’bad, and Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Rather, the matter of Al-Aqra’ bin Habis, so Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: You only wanted to contradict me, so Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I did not want to contradict you, so they argued until their voices rose, and then the following verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger until the verse was completed, And if they had been patient until you came out to them… And thus he narrated it here alone as well. And Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Al-Fadl bin Sahl told us, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, Husayn bin Umar told us, on the authority of Mukhariq, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed, O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, I said: O Messenger of God, by God I will not speak to you except as a confidential brother. Husayn bin Umar, even though this is weak, we have narrated it from the hadith of Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf and Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with them in a similar manner, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Azhar bin Saad told us, Ibn Awn told us, Musa bin Anas told me, on the authority of Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) missed Thabit bin Qais may God be pleased with him, so a man said: O Messenger of God, I know what you know. So he went to him and found him in his house with his head bowed. So he said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: Evil was raising his voice above the voice of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. His deeds have been nullified and he is one of the people of Hellfire. So the man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him that he had said such and such. Moses said: So he returned to him a second time with great glad tidings and said: Go to him and tell him that you are not one of the people of Hellfire but one of the people of Paradise. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted this from this source. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim told us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet until His saying while you perceive not, Thabit ibn Qays ibn al-Shammas had a loud voice, so he said: I am the one who used to raise my voice to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I am one of the people of Hell. My deeds have been in vain, and he sat with his family, sad, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, missed him. Some of the people went to him and said to him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, missed you. What is wrong with you? He said: I am the one who raises my voice above the voice of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I say to him loudly: My deeds have been in vain. I am one of the people of Hell. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what he had said. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, rather he is one of the people of Paradise. Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: We used to see him walking among us and we knew that he was one of the people of Paradise. Then, on the day of Yamamah, we were somewhat dismayed, so Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas came, and he had embalmed himself and put on his shroud. He said: How evil is what you do to your peers. So he fought them until he was killed, may God be pleased with him. Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit Al-Bunani, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet to the end of the verse, Thabit, may God be pleased with him, sat in his house and said: I am one of the people of Hellfire, and he was kept away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Sa`d ibn Mu`adh: O Abu `Amr, what is the matter with Thabit that he is complaining? Sa`d, may God be pleased with him, said: He is my neighbor and I do not know of any complaint from him.” He said: Saad may God be pleased with him came to him and mentioned to him the statement of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Thabit may God be pleased with him said: This verse was revealed, and you know that I am the one among you who raises my voice to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so I am one of the people of Hellfire. Saad may God be pleased with him mentioned that to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Rather, he is one of the people of Paradise. Then Muslim narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Sa’id al-Darami on the authority of Hayyan ibn Hilal on the authority of Sulayman ibn al-Mughira with this chain of transmission, and he said that Saad ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him was not mentioned. It was also narrated on the authority of Qatan ibn Bashir on the authority of Ja’far ibn Sulayman on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him in a similar manner, and he said that it does not mention Saad ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him. Hudbah ibn ‘Abd al-A’la al-Asadi told me, on the authority of al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, I heard my father mentioning on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him who said: When this verse was revealed, he cut the story short and did not mention Saad ibn Mu’adh may God be pleased with him. He added: We used to see a man from the people of Paradise walking among us. These three methods explain the narration of Hammad bin Salamah in what he mentioned alone of Sa`d bin Mu`adh, may God be pleased with him. The correct view is that when this verse was revealed, Sa`d bin Mu`adh, may God be pleased with him, was not present, because he had died a few days after Banu Qurayzah in the year five. These verses were revealed regarding the delegation of Banu Tamim, and the delegations only came in succession in the year nine of the Hijra, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Zaid bin Al-Hubab told us, Abu Thabit bin Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas told us, my uncle Ismail bin Muhammad bin Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas told me on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed, Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or be loud to him in speech, Thabit bin Qais, may God be pleased with him, sat in the road weeping. Asim bin Adi from Banu Al-Ajlan passed by him and said: What makes you cry, Thabit? He said: I fear that this verse was revealed about me, as I have a loud voice. He said: Asim bin Adi, may God be pleased with him, went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Weeping overcame him, so he went to his wife, Jamila, daughter of Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and said to her: When you enter my horse’s house, tie a nail to the rein. So she hit him with a nail until he came out, and he turned away and said: I will not come out until God, the Most High, takes me, or the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased with me. He said: Asim, may God be pleased with him, came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him his story. He said: Go and call him to me. So Asim, may God be pleased with him, came to the place but did not find him, so he came to his family and found him in the horse’s house. He said to him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is calling you. He said: Break the rein. He said: So they went out and came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What makes you cry, Thabit? He may God be pleased with him said: I am well-known and I fear that this verse was revealed regarding: Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, nor speak loudly to him. The Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: Are you not satisfied to live a life of praise, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise? He said: “I am satisfied with the glad tidings of God Almighty and His Messenger, and I will never raise my voice above the voice of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace).” He said: And God the Almighty revealed: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God - it is those whose hearts God has tested for piety Al-Akhbar 2:17. This story was also mentioned by more than one of the Successors, as God the Almighty forbade raising voices in the presence of the Messenger of God. And the Almighty said: lest your deeds be rendered worthless while you perceive not. And he does not act upon it, so Omar, may God be pleased with him, wrote: Those who desire sin but do not act upon it, Those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety - for them is forgiveness and a great reward.
49:4: Then He, the Blessed and Exalted, condemned those who call Him from behind the rooms, which are the houses of His wives, as the ignorant Bedouins do, saying: Most of them do not use reason. Then He, the Exalted, guided us to proper etiquette in that, saying: And if only they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. That is, it would have been good and beneficial for them in this world and the hereafter. Then He, the Exalted, said, calling them to repentance and turning back: And God is Forgiving and Merciful. It has been mentioned that it was revealed about Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis Al-Tamimi, may God be pleased with him, according to what was reported by more than one person. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Musa bin Uqbah told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Aqra’ bin Habis, may God be pleased with him, that he called out to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from behind the rooms and said: O Muhammad, O Muhammad. In another narration: O Messenger of God. But he did not answer him, so he said: O Messenger of God, my praise is adornment and my blame is ugliness. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is God, the Almighty and Majestic. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Ammar al-Husayn bin Harith al-Marwazi told us, al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Bara’, regarding the words of God, the Most High: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the rooms he said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, my praise is adornment and my blame is ugliness. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is God, the Almighty and Majestic. Al-Hasan al-Basri and Qatada mentioned it in a mursal manner. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Umrah who said: Bishr ibn Ghalib and Labid ibn Uttar or Bishr ibn Uttar and Labid ibn Ghalib were sitting with al-Hajjaj when Bishr ibn Ghalib said to al-Bud ibn Uttar: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers… was revealed about your people, Banu Tamim. I mentioned that to Sa’id ibn Jubayr who said: If he had known the end of the verse, he would have answered: They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. They said: We became Muslims and Banu Asad did not fight you. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Amr ibn Ali al-Bahili narrated to us, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard Dawud al-Tafawi narrating on the authority of Abu Muslim al-Bajali on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam may God be pleased with him who said: Some Arabs gathered and said: Let us go to this man. If he is a prophet, we will be the luckiest people to have him, and if he is a king, we will live in his wings. He said: So I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of what they had said. They came to the room of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and began to call out to him while he was in his room: O Muhammad, O Muhammad. Then God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the rooms, most of them do not use reason. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took hold of my ear and stretched it out and began to say: “God, the Most High, has fulfilled your word, O Zayd. God, the Most High, has fulfilled your word, O Zayd.” Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Arfa, on the authority of Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman on his authority.

49:6: God Almighty orders verification of the report of a sinner to be on the safe side lest he judges based on his words, which would in fact be a liar or mistaken, and thus the one who judges based on his words would have followed his example. God Almighty has forbidden following the path of the corruptors. Hence, some groups of scholars refrained from accepting the report of someone whose status is unknown due to the possibility of his being a sinner in reality. Others accepted it because we were only ordered to verify the report of a sinner, and this person is not definitely a sinner because his status is unknown. We have established this issue in the Book of Knowledge from the explanation of Al-Bukhari, and all praise and thanks are due to God Almighty. Many commentators have mentioned that this verse was revealed regarding Al-Walid bin Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to collect the alms of Banu Al-Mustaliq. This has been narrated through various chains of narration, the best of which is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad from the narration of the king of Banu Al-Mustaliq, who was Al-Harith bin Dirar, the father of Juwayriya bint Al-Harith, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Sabeq told us, Isa ibn Dinar told us, my father told me that he heard Al-Harith ibn Dirar Al-Khuza’i may God be pleased with him say: I came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he invited me to Islam, so I entered it and acknowledged it. He invited me to pay zakat, so I acknowledged it and said: O Messenger of God, let me go back to them and invite them to Islam and to pay zakat. Whoever responds to me, I will collect his zakat. And send me, O Messenger of God, a messenger at such and such a time to bring you what I have collected of zakat. When Al-Harith collected the zakat from those who responded to him and the time came that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wanted to send to him, the messenger was delayed and did not come to him. Al-Harith thought that he had caused displeasure with God Almighty and His Messenger, so he called the leaders of his people and said to them, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had set a time for me to send his messenger to me to collect what I had of zakat, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has no way of breaking it, and I do not think that he detained his messenger except out of displeasure.” So let us go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Al-Walid ibn Uqbah to Al-Harith to collect what he had of the zakat he had collected. When Al-Walid traveled until he reached some of the road, he became afraid, so he returned until he came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, O Messenger of God, Al-Harith has prevented me from the zakat and wants to kill me. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) became angry and sent the delegation to Al-Harith may God be pleased with him. Al-Harith came with his companions until the delegation arrived and departed from Madinah. Al-Harith met them and they said, This is Al-Harith. When he… He deceived them and said to them: To whom have you been sent? They said: To you. He said: Why? They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Walid ibn Uqba to you. He claimed that you withheld the zakat from him and wanted to kill him. God the Almighty said: And know that among you is the Messenger of God meaning, know that among you is the Messenger of God, so honor him, respect him, be polite with him, and submit to his command, for he knows what is best for you and is more concerned about you than you are, and his opinion of you is more perfect than your opinion of yourselves, as God the Almighty said: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves. Then He explained that their opinion is ridiculous in relation to their own interests, saying: If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in distress, meaning, if he were to obey you in everything you choose, this would lead to your distress and hardship, as God the Almighty said: “And if the truth had followed their inclinations, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been ruined. Rather, We have brought them their message, but from its message they turn away.” God the Almighty said: But God has endeared faith to you and made it pleasing in your hearts, meaning, He has made it beloved to your souls and made it beautiful in your hearts. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz told us, Ali bin Mas`adah told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to say: Islam is outward and faith is in the heart. Then he pointed to his chest three times and said: Piety is here, piety is here. “And He has made hateful to you disbelief, immorality, and disobedience.” That is, He has made hateful to you disbelief, immorality, and disobedience, which are major sins, and disobedience, which are all transgressions. This is a gradation of the perfection of the blessing. And the Most High said: Those are the ones who are rightly guided. That is, those who are described by this characteristic are the rightly guided to whom God has given their right guidance. Imam Ahmad said: Marwan bin Muawiyah Al-Fazari narrated to us, Abdul Wahid bin Ayman Al-Makki narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rifa’ah Al-Zarqi, on the authority of his father, who said: When the Battle of Uhud took place and the polytheists retreated, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Line up so that I may praise my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime. So they stood in rows behind him, and he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O God, all praise is due to You. O God, there is no one who can withhold what You have granted, nor grant what You have withheld, nor guide whom You have led astray, nor lead astray whom You have guided, nor give what You have withheld, nor withhold what You have given, nor bring near what You have distanced, nor distance what You have brought near. O God, bestow upon us from Your blessings, mercy, favor, and provision. O God, I ask You for lasting bliss that does not change or disappear. O God, I ask You for bliss on the day of poverty and security on the day of fear. O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You have given us and from the evil of what You have withheld from us. O God, endear faith to us and adorn it in our hearts, and make disbelief, immorality, and disobedience hateful to us, and make us among the rightly guided.” O God “Cause we die as Muslims and bring us back to life as Muslims and join us with the righteous, neither disgraced nor afflicted. O God, fight the disbelievers who deny Your messengers and avert [people] from Your path and inflict upon them Your punishment and torment. O God, fight the disbelievers who were given the Scripture, O God, the God of truth.” Narrated by An-Nasa’i in Al-Yawm wal-Laylah on the authority of Ziyad ibn Ayyub, on the authority of Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Rifa’ah, on the authority of his father, with this chain of transmission. And in the authentic hadith: Whoever is pleased with his good deeds and displeased with his bad deeds is a believer. Then he said: A bounty from God and a blessing, meaning this gift that He has given you is a bounty from Him to you and a blessing from Him. And God is Knowing and Wise, meaning He is All-Knowing of who deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance. He is Wise in His words and deeds, His law and His power.
49:9: God the Almighty says, commanding reconciliation between the two groups that transgress against each other: And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make settlement between them. So He called them believers despite the fighting. Al-Bukhari and others used this as evidence that one does not leave the faith because of a sin, no matter how great, unlike what the Khawarij and those who followed them from the Mu’tazila and others say. This is also proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari from the hadith of Al-Hasan from Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) delivered a sermon one day, and with him on the pulpit was Al-Hasan ibn Ali may God be pleased with them both. He looked at him one time and at the people another time and said: This son of mine is a master, and perhaps God the Almighty will reconcile between two great groups of Muslims through him. And it was as he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said. God reconciled between the people of Ash-Sham and the people of Iraq through him after the long wars and horrific events. God the Almighty said: But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of God. That is, until it returns to the command of God and His Messenger, and listens to the truth and obeys it, as was proven in the Sahih on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Support your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. I said: O Messenger of God, this is supporting him when he is oppressed, but how do I support him when he is an oppressor? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Preventing him from oppression is like supporting him. Imam Ahmad said: Aarem told us, Mu'tamir told us: I heard my father narrating that Anas may God be pleased with him said: It was said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Why don’t you go to Abdullah ibn Ubayy? So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to him and rode a donkey, and the Muslims set off walking, and it was marshy land. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to him, he said, Go away from me, for by God, the smell of your donkey has bothered me. A man from the Ansar said, “By God, the smell of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)’s donkey is better than yours.” Some men from his people became angry on Abdullah’s behalf, and so did their companions. He said: There was fighting between them with palm branches, hands, and sandals, and it reached us that the verse was revealed about them: “And if two parties among the believers should quarrel, then make peace between them.” Al-Bukhari narrated it in Al-Sulh on the authority of Musaddad, and Muslim in Al-Maghazi on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la, both of them on the authority of al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, on the authority of his father, with a similar wording. Saeed bin Jubair mentioned that there was a fight between the Aws and the Khazraj with palm leaves and sandals, so God revealed this verse and ordered reconciliation between them. Al-Suddi said: There was a man from the Ansar called Imran, who had a wife called Umm Zaid. The woman wanted to visit her family, but her husband imprisoned her and placed her in his upper room, and none of her family could enter upon her. The woman sent word to her family, and her people came and let her stay so that they could take her. The man had gone out, so the man’s family sought help, but his cousins came to stand between the woman and her family, and they pushed each other and fought with sandals, so this verse was revealed about them. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent word to them and reconciled them, and they returned to the command of God. God the Almighty said: {But if they return, then make peace between them with justice and act justly. Indeed, God loves those who act justly.} meaning, treat them justly regarding what some of them had done to others with justice, which is for God loves those who act justly. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The just in this world will be on pulpits of pearls in front of the Most Merciful, the Almighty, because of their justice in this world. An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, on the authority of Abd al-A’la with it. The chain of transmission of this chain is good and its men are strong according to the criteria of the Sahih. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Amr ibn Aws, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The just in the sight of God, the Most High, on the Day of Resurrection will be on pulpits of light to the right of the Throne, those who are just in their judgment, with their families, and with those under their care.” Muslim and an-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah with it. God the Almighty says: The believers are but brothers, meaning all are brothers in religion, as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “A Muslim is a brother to a Muslim. He does not wrong him nor does he hand him over.” In the Sahih: God helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother. In the Sahih also: When a Muslim prays for his brother in his absence, the angel says, ‘Amen, and for you the same.’ There are many hadiths on this. In the Sahih: “The example of the believers in their mutual love, mercy, and communication is like that of a single body. If one part of it is ill, the rest of the body feels pain and sleeplessness.” In the Sahih also: The believer to the believer is like a building, whose parts support one another. And he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) interlaced his fingers. Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj told us, Abdullah told us, Mus`ab ibn Thabit told us, Abu Hazim told me: I heard Sahl ibn Sa`d al-Sa`idi may God be pleased with him narrating on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who said: “The believer is to the people of faith as the head is to the body. The believer feels pain for the people of faith just as the body feels pain for the head.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and its chain of transmission is sound. God the Almighty says: So make settlement between your two brothers, meaning the two warring factions. And fear God, meaning in all your affairs, that you may receive mercy. This is a confirmation from God the Almighty of mercy for those who fear Him.
