49:11: God the Almighty forbids mocking people, which means belittling and mocking them, as it was proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people - and it was narrated - and looking down on people. What is meant by that is looking down on them and belittling them, and this is forbidden, because the one being looked down upon may be of greater standing with God the Almighty, and more beloved to Him than the one being mocked and looked down upon. For this reason God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. So He explicitly forbade men, and conjoined the prohibition of women. And God the Almighty said: And do not insult one another meaning do not insult people. The slanderer and backbiter among men is condemned and cursed, as God Almighty said: Woe to every slanderer and backbiter. Slander is by action and backbiting is by speech, as God Almighty said: A slanderer, going about with calumnies, meaning he despises people and backbites them, oppressing them and walking among them with gossip, which is backbiting by speech. For this reason He said here: And do not backbite one another, as He said: And do not kill one another, meaning do not kill one another. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Qatadah and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: And do not insult one another means do not insult one another. God the Almighty said: And do not call one another by nicknames means do not call one another by nicknames that are unpleasant to hear. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Abu Jubayrah bin Ad-Dahhak told me, he said: And do not call one another by nicknames was revealed about us, Banu Salamah. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Madinah and there was not a man among us who did not have two or three names. If he called one of them by one of those names, they would say: O Messenger of God, this angers him. So, And do not call one another by nicknames was revealed. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Musa bin Ismail, on the authority of Wahib, on the authority of Dawud, with this same meaning. God the Almighty said: How evil is the name of immorality after faith means how evil is the description and name of immorality. It is the exchange of nicknames as the people of the Age of Ignorance used to exchange nicknames after you entered Islam and understood it. And whoever does not repent from this, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
49:12: The Almighty says, forbidding His believing servants from much suspicion, which is accusation and betrayal of family, relatives and people without justification, because some of that is pure sin, so much of it should be avoided as a precaution. We have narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Do not think anything but good of a word that comes out of your believing brother, even if you find a good interpretation for it. Abu Abdullah ibn Majah said: Abu al-Qasim ibn Abi Damrah Nasr ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Himsi told us, my father told us, Abdullah ibn Abi Qays al-Nadri told us, Abdullah ibn Umar may God be pleased with them both told us: I saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) circumambulating the Kaaba and saying: “How fragrant you are and how fragrant your scent is! How great you are and how great is your sanctity! By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, the sanctity of the believer is greater in the sight of God than your sanctity: his wealth and his blood, and that he should be thought of only good.” Ibn Majah is the only one to narrate it from this chain of narration. Malik said, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of al-A’raj, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the falsest of speech. Do not spy, do not seek out faults, do not compete with one another, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, and do not turn your backs on one another. Be, O servants of God, brothers.” Narrated by al-Bukhari on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yusuf, and by Muslim on the authority of Yahya ibn Yahya, and by Abu Dawud on the authority of al-Utbi, on the authority of Malik. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated from Az-Zuhri from Anas may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not boycott one another, do not turn away from one another, do not hate one another, and do not envy one another. Be, O servants of God, brothers. It is not permissible for a Muslim to abandon his brother for more than three days.” Narrated by Muslim and At-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. At-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah Al-Qarmati Al-Adawi narrated to us, Bakr ibn Abdul-Wahhab Al-Madani narrated to us, Ismail ibn Qays Al-Ansari narrated to us, Abdul-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Al-Rijal narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather Haritha ibn An-Nu’man may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Three things will be a constant companion of my ummah: superstition, envy, and suspicion.” The man said: How can they be removed, O Messenger of God, from someone who has them? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “If you feel envy, then seek forgiveness from God. If you suspect something, then do not investigate. If you have superstitions, then move on.” Abu Dawud said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, from al-A’mash, from Zayd may God be pleased with him, who said: A man was brought to Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, and it was said to him: This is so-and-so, whose beard is dripping with wine. Abdullah may God be pleased with him said: We have been forbidden from spying, but if something appears to us, we will act upon it. Ibn Abi Hatim named him in his narration: al-Walid ibn Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Nasheet al-Khawlani, from Ka’b ibn Alqamah, from Abu al-Haytham, from Dukhayn, the scribe of Uqbah, who said: I said to Uqbah: We have neighbors who drink wine, and I am going to call the police to arrest them. He said: Do not do that, but admonish them and threaten them. So he did that, but they did not desist. He said: Then Dukhayn came to him and said: I forbade them but they did not stop, and I am going to call the police to arrest them. Uqbah said to him: Woe to you! Why don’t you do that? I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: Whoever covers the private parts of a believer, it is as if he has saved a buried girl from her grave. Abu Dawud and An-Nasa’i narrated it similarly from the hadith of Al-Layth ibn Sa’d. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said from Thawr from Rashid ibn Sa’d from Mu’awiyah may God be pleased with him who said: I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: If you pursue the private parts of people, you will corrupt them or almost corrupt them. Abu Ad-Darda’ may God be pleased with him said a statement that Mu’awiyah may God be pleased with him heard from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and God benefited him with it. Abu Dawud narrated it alone from the hadith of Ath-Thawri. Abu Dawud also said: Saeed bin Amr Al-Hadrami narrated to us, Ismail bin Ayyash narrated to us, Damdam bin Zar’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubaid, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, Kathir bin Murrah, Amr bin Al-Aswad, Al-Miqdam bin Ma’dikarib, and Abu Umamah may God be pleased with them that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If a ruler seeks to cast doubt on the people, he will corrupt them. “And do not spy” means on one another. Spying is often used to mean evil, including the word spy. As for finding out, it is usually used for good, as God the Almighty said, reporting on the authority of Jacob, that he said: O my sons, go and find out about Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of relief from God. Both of them may be used for evil, as it is proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not spy, do not find out about one another, do not hate one another, and do not turn your backs on one another. And be, O servants of God, brothers.” Al-Awza’i said: Spying means searching for something. Eavesdropping means listening to people’s conversations when they are reluctant to do so, or eavesdropping on their doors. And turning away means cutting off ties. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on his authority. God the Almighty says: And let not some of you backbite others in it is a prohibition against backbiting. The Lawgiver has interpreted it as it came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud: Al-Qa’nabi told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: It was said, O Messenger of God, what is backbiting? He said, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: Mentioning your brother in a way that he dislikes. It was said: What if what I say is in my brother? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If what you say is true, then you have backbitten him, and if what you say is not true, then you have slandered him. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of Ad-Darawardi, who said: It is hasan saheeh. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Ghandar on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Al-Ala’. This is what Ibn ‘Umar may God be pleased with them both said, as did Masruq, Qatadah, Abu Ishaq, and Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah. Abu Dawud said: Musaddad told us, Yahya told us on the authority of Sufyan, Ali ibn Al-Aqmar told me on the authority of Abu Hudhayfah on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: I said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Such and such is enough for you from Safiyyah. Other than Musaddad, he meant short. So he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You have said a word which, if it were mixed with the water of the sea, it would mix it. She said: “And I described a person to him, so he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I would not like to have described a person even though I have such and such.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Yahya Al-Qattan, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, and Waki’, all three of them on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Ali ibn Al-Aqmar, on the authority of Abu Hudhayfah. Salamah bin Suhaib Al-Arhabi, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: It is good and authentic. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told me, Abd Al-Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, Hassan bin Al-Mukhariq told us that a woman entered upon Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and when she stood up to leave, Aisha, may God be pleased with her, pointed with her hand to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that she was short. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, You have backbitten her. Backbiting is forbidden by consensus, and no exception is made from it except for those whose interests are more likely, as in Al-Jarh wa Al-Ta’dil and Al-Nasiyah, like his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, when that wicked man asked permission to enter: Give him permission, what a bad brother of the tribe! And as he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Fatimah bint Qais may God be pleased with her, when Muawiyah and Abu al-Jahm proposed to her: As for Muawiyah, he is a vagabond, and as for Abu al-Jahm, he will not let his staff down from his shoulder. And so on, and the rest of it is based on severe mercy, and it contains a firm warning. That is why God, the Blessed and Exalted, likened it to eating the flesh of a dead person, as He, the Almighty, said: Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it. That is, just as you hate this naturally, hate that according to Islamic law, because its punishment is more severe than this. This is an example of alienation from it and a warning against it, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about the one who takes back his gift: Like a dog that vomits and then returns to its vomit. And he said: We have no bad example. And it is proven in the Sahihs, Hassans, and Musnads from more than one source that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the Farewell Sermon: Your blood, your wealth, and your honor are sacred to you, as sacred as this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours. Abu Dawud said: Wasil ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Asbat ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The entirety of a Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his wealth, his honour and his blood. It is enough evil for a man to look down on his Muslim brother.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, and he said: It is hasan ghareeb. Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us: Al-Aswad ibn Amir told us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abdullah ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abu Barzah Al-Aslami, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O you who have believed with your tongues but faith has not entered your hearts, do not backbite the Muslims and do not pursue their faults, for whoever pursues their faults, God will pursue his faults, and whoever God pursues his faults, He will disgrace him in his own home.” Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn Azib. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said in his Musnad: Ibrahim bin Dinar told us, Mus`ab bin Salam told us, on the authority of Hamza bin Habib al-Zayyat, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi`i, on the authority of al-Bara` bin `Azib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us, so that the young girls could hear it in their homes - or he said - in their chambers. He said: O group of people who believe with their tongues, do not backbite the Muslims and do not pursue their faults, for whoever pursues the faults of his brother, God will pursue his faults, and whoever God pursues his faults, He will disgrace him in the interior of his home. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Umar. Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Ismaili said: Abdullah bin Najiyah told us, Yahya bin Aktham told us, Al-Fadl bin Musa Al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Waqid, on the authority of Awfa bin Dahlam, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O group of people who have believed with their tongues but faith has not yet reached their hearts, do not backbite the Muslims and do not pursue their faults, for whoever pursues the faults of the Muslims, God will pursue his faults, and whoever God pursues his faults, He will disgrace him even if it is in the interior of his home.” He said: One day Ibn Umar looked at the Kaaba and said: How great you are and how great is your sanctity, and the believer has greater sanctity before God than you. Abu Dawud said: Haywah ibn Shuraih narrated to us, Qutaybah narrated to us, from Ibn Thauban, from his father, from Mahkul, from Waqqas ibn Rabi’ah, from Al-Mustawrid, that he told him that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever eats a meal in the name of a Muslim, God will feed him the like of it in Hell. Whoever covers a Muslim with a garment, God will clothe him in the like of it in Hell. Whoever stands in a position of showing off and ostentation in the name of a man, God will stand in a position of showing off and ostentation in his place on the Day of Resurrection.” This is narrated only by Abu Dawud. Ibn Musaffa narrated to us, from Baqiyyah and Abu Al-Mughira, from Safwan, from Rashid ibn Sa’d and Abd Al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When I was taken up to heaven, I passed by people who had nails of copper with which they were scratching their faces and chests. I said: ‘Who are these, O Gabriel?’ He said: ‘These are the ones who eat the flesh of people and slander them.’” This is narrated only by Abu Dawud. Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Abu Al-Mughira Abd Al-Quddus ibn Al-Hajjaj Al-Shami. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad bin Abdah told us, Abu Abd al-Samad Abd al-Aziz bin Abd al-Samad al-Ami told us, Abu Harun al-Abdi told us on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri who said: We said, O Messenger of God, tell us what you saw on the night of your Ascension. He said: Then I was taken to a large group of God’s creation, men and women, with men assigned to them. They would go to the side of one of them and cut off a piece of it like a sandal and then put it in the mouth of one of them. It would be said to him, ‘Eat as you have eaten,’ and he would find death in eating it. O Muhammad, if only he could find death even though it was forced upon him. I said, ‘O Gabriel, who are these?’ He said: These are the backbiters and slanderers, the gossipers. It is said: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it, but he is hated to eat his flesh. This is how this hadith was reported, and we have cited it in full at the beginning of the interpretation of Surat Subhan. To God be praise and thanks. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded the people to fast one day and that no one should break his fast until he gave him permission. So the people fasted, and when evening came, a man would come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: I have been fasting since today, so give me permission to break my fast. So he gave him permission. Another man would come and say that, and he would give him permission until a man came and said: O Messenger of God, two women from your family have been fasting since today, so give them permission to break their fast. So he turned away from him, then he repeated it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They have not fasted, and how can someone who has been eating people’s flesh fast? Go and order them, if they are fasting, to vomit. So they did, and each one vomited. From them was a clot, so he went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If they had died while they were in them, the Fire would have consumed them. A weak chain of transmission and a strange text. Al-Hafiz al-Bayhaqi narrated it on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun. Sulayman al-Taymi narrated: I heard a man narrating in the assembly of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, on the authority of Ubayd, the freed slave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), that two women fasted during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and that a man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, there are two women here who are fasting and they are almost dying of thirst. I think he said during the middle of the day. So he turned away from him or remained silent. Then he said: O Prophet of God, by God they have died or are almost dying. So he said: Call them. So they came. A cup or a bowl was brought, and he said to one of them: Vomit. She vomited pus, blood, and feces until she had vomited half the cup. Then he said to the other, Vomit. So she vomited pus, blood, feces, flesh, and other things until she had filled the cup. Then he said, “These two fasted from what God made lawful for them and broke their fast with what God made unlawful for them. One of them sat next to the other and they began to eat the flesh of people.” This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it from Yazid ibn Harun and Ibn Abi Udayy, both of them from Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi with a similar or similar narration. Then he also narrated it from the hadith of Musaddad from Yahya al-Qattan from Uthman ibn Ghiyath. A man, I think he was in the circle of Abu Uthman, told me from Sa’d, the freed slave of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), that they were ordered to fast. A man came at noon and said, O Messenger of God, so-and-so and so-and-so have reached the point of exhaustion. He turned away from him two or three times, then said, Leave them. So he brought a bowl or a cup and said to one of them, Vomit. She vomited thick flesh, blood, and pus. He said the same to the other, then said: These two kept silent about what God had made lawful for them and broke their fast with what God had forbidden them. One of them came to the other, and they continued to eat the flesh of people until their stomachs were filled with pus. Al-Bayhaqi said: This is what he said on the authority of Sa`d, but the first, which is `Ubayd, is more authentic. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Amr ibn al-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad narrated to us, my father narrated to us, my father Abu Asim narrated to us, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me, on the authority of a cousin of Abu Hurayrah, that Ma’iz came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, I have committed adultery. He turned away from him until he said it four times. When he had said it the fifth time, he said: Do you know what adultery is? He said: Yes, I committed it unlawfully, just as a man does to his wife lawfully. He said: What do you want me to say? He said: I want you to purify me. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Did you introduce that from you into it from her, just as a whisk disappears into a kohl container or a rope into a well? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: So he ordered that he be stoned, and he was stoned. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard two men, one of them saying to the other: Have you not seen this man whom God concealed, yet he did not let himself leave him until he was stoned like a dog? Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) walked on until he passed by the carcass of a donkey and said: Where are so-and-so and so-and-so? Get off and eat from the carcass of this donkey. They said: May God forgive you, O Messenger of God! Is this permissible to eat? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “What you did to your brother just now is more detrimental to eating than this. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, he is now in the rivers of Paradise, immersing himself in them.” Sahih chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad told us, my father told me, Wasil, the freed slave of Ibn Uyaynah told us, Khalid ibn Urfata told me, on the authority of Talha ibn Nafi’, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a foul odor of a dead body arose. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know what this odor is? This is the odor of those who backbite people. Another path Abd bin Hamid said in his Musnad: Ibrahim bin Al-Ash’ath told us, Al-Fudayl bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, who is Talha bin Nafi’, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, and a foul wind blew. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A group of hypocrites have backbitten some Muslims, and that is why this wind was sent. Or he might have said: That is why this wind blew. Al-Suddi said regarding the words of God Almighty: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? He claimed that Salman Al-Farsi, may God be pleased with him, was with two men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, serving them, helping them, and eating from their food. And that when Salman, may God be pleased with him, the people traveled one day, and Salman, may God be pleased with him, remained asleep and did not travel with them, his two companions began to talk to him, but they did not find him, so they pitched the tent and said: Neither Salman nor this servant wants anything other than this, that he comes to prepared food and a pitched tent. So when Salman came They sent him to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to ask for some food for them. He went and came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) carrying a cup of his and said: O Messenger of God, my companions have sent me to provide them with some food if you have any. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: What do your companions do with the food? They have already had some food. Salman may God be pleased with him returned and told them what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had said. They went until they came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: By Him who sent you with the truth, we have not had any food since we came down. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You have already had some food with Salman because of what you said. He said: Then the verse was revealed: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? He said: He was asleep. Al-Hafiz Al-Dhiya’ Al-Maqdisi narrated in his book Al-Mukhtar, on the authority of Hubban bin Hilal, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Arabs used to serve each other on journeys. There was a man with Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, who was serving them. They slept and woke up, and he had not prepared food for them. They said: This man is sleeping. So they woke him up and said to him: Go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and tell him that Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, send you their greetings and ask you to serve them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They have eaten food. They came and said: O Messenger of God, what should we eat as food? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “By the flesh of your brother. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I see his flesh between your teeth.” They said, may God be pleased with them both, Ask forgiveness for us, O Messenger of God. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Tell him to ask forgiveness for you both. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Al-Hakam bin Musa told us, Muhammad bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of his uncle Musa bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Whoever eats of his brother’s flesh in this world, God will bring his flesh near to him in the Hereafter, and it will be said to him, ‘Eat it dead as you ate it alive. ’ He will eat it, chew it, and cry out.” Very strange. God the Almighty said: And fear God meaning in what He has commanded you to do and what He has forbidden you, so observe Him in that and fear Him. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful meaning, He is Forgiving to those who repent to Him, and Merciful to those who return to Him and rely on Him. The majority of scholars said: The way for a backbiter to repent is for him to stop doing that and resolve never to do it again. Is regret for what has passed a condition? There is a dispute about this. He should also seek forgiveness from the one he backbitten. Others said: It is not a condition that he apologizes, because if he informs him of that, he may be more hurt than if he did not know what he did. So his way is to praise him for what he did in the gatherings in which he used to criticize him, and to respond to the backbiting according to his ability, so that the former will be for the latter, as Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj told us, Abdullah told us, Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sulayman, that Ismail ibn Yahya al-Ma’afiri told him, that Sahl ibn Mu’adh ibn Anas al-Juhani told him, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: “Whoever protects a believer from a hypocrite who backbites him, God the Most High will send to him an angel who will protect his flesh from the fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. And whoever accuses a believer of something intending to insult him, God the Most High will imprison him on the bridge of Hell until he comes out of what he said.” Abu Dawud also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah, who is Ibn al-Mubarak, in a similar manner. Abu Dawud also said: Ishaq bin Al-Sabah told us, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Al-Layth told us, Yahya bin Saleem told me that he heard Ismail bin Bashir say: I heard Jabir bin Abdullah and Abu Talha bin Sahl Al-Ansari, may God be pleased with them, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no man who abandons a Muslim leader in a situation where his sanctity is violated and his honor is diminished, except that God Almighty will abandon him in situations where he would like to be aided. And there is no man who supports a Muslim leader in a situation where his honor is diminished and his sanctity is violated, except that God Almighty will support him in situations where he would like to be aided.” Narrated only by Abu Dawud.
49:13: The Almighty says, informing people that He created them from one soul and made from it its mate, namely Adam and Eve, and made them peoples, which is more general than tribes. After the tribes are other ranks such as factions, clans, buildings, thighs, and others. It was said that what is meant by peoples are the clans of the Persians, and by tribes are the clans of the Arabs, just as the tribes are the clans of the Children of Israel. I have summarized this in a separate introduction that I collected from the book Al-Inbah by Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr, and from the book Al-Qasd and Al-Umam in Knowing the Genealogies of the Arabs and Persians. All people are equal in honor in relation to Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, and they only differ in religious matters, which are obedience to God Almighty and following His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. For this reason, the Almighty said, after forbidding backbiting and some people despising others, pointing out their equality in humanity: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another meaning that acquaintance may occur between them, each one going back to his tribe. Mujahid said in The Almighty said, So that you may know one another, just as one says, So-and-so, son of so-and-so, is from such-and-such tribe. Sufyan al-Thawri said, The Himyar people traced their lineage back to their districts, and the Arabs of the Hijaz traced their lineage back to their tribes. Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi said, “Ahmad ibn Muhammad told us, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Isa al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba’ith, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said, ‘Learn from your genealogies that by which you may maintain kinship ties, for maintaining kinship ties brings love among family, increases wealth, and prolongs life.” Then he said, It is strange, and we do not know it except from this source. God the Almighty says: The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. This means that you are distinguished before God the Almighty by righteousness, not by lineage. Hadiths have been reported on this matter from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Salam told us, Abdah told us, on the authority of Ubaydullah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Sa’id may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked, Which people are the most honorable? He said, The most honorable of them in the sight of God is the most righteous of them. They said, We are not asking you about this. He said, The most honorable of people is Joseph, the Prophet of God, the son of the Prophet of God, the son of the Prophet of God, the son of the Friend of God. They said, We are not asking you about this. He said, Do you ask me about the origins of the Arabs? They said, Yes. He said, The best of you in the pre-Islamic period are the best of you in Islam if they attain understanding. Al-Bukhari narrated it in more than one place through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abdah ibn Sulayman, and Al-Nasa’i narrated it in his Tafsir from the hadith of Ubaydullah, who is Ibn ‘Umar Al-‘Umari, with the same chain of transmission. Another hadith Muslim, may God have mercy on him, said: Amr al-Naqid told us, Katheer bin Hisham told us, Jaafar bin Burqan told us, on the authority of Yazid bin al-Asamm, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God does not look at your appearances and your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Sinan, on the authority of Katheer bin Hisham, with the same chain of transmission. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Bakr, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Look, you are not better than a red man or a black man unless you excel him in your fear of God. Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, transmitted it alone. Another hadith Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Abu Ubaidah Abdul-Warith bin Ibrahim Al-Askari told us, Abdul-Rahman bin Amr bin Jabalah told us, Ubaid bin Hunayn Al-Ta’i told us, I heard Muhammad bin Habib bin Kharash Al-Asri narrating on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Muslims are brothers, no one has superiority over anyone else except in piety. Another Hadith Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Ahmad bin Yahya Al-Kufi told us, Al-Hasan bin Al-Hussain told us, Qais - meaning Ibn Al-Rabi’ - told us, on the authority of Shabib bin Gharqadah, on the authority of Al-Mustazil bin Husayn, on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You are all children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust. Let a people who boast about their fathers stop, or they will be more insignificant to God Almighty than jerks.” Then he said: We do not know it from Hudhayfah except through this source. Another hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, Asad bin Musa told us, Yahya bin Zakariya Al-Qattan told us, Musa bin Ubaydah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated Mecca on the day of the conquest of Mecca on his she-camel Al-Qaswa’, touching the corners with a stick in his hand. He did not find a place for it to kneel in the mosque until he, may God bless him and grant him peace, dismounted at the hands of the men. He went out with it to the bottom of the torrent and it was made to kneel. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed them on his mount, praising God Almighty and extolling Him as He deserved, then he said: “O people, God Almighty has removed from you the shame of the Age of Ignorance and its glorification of its forefathers. People are of two types: a righteous, pious man who is honored by God Almighty, and a wicked, wretched man who is insignificant by God Almighty. God Almighty says: ‘O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. Indeed, God is Knowing and Acquainted.’” Then he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I say this and ask God for forgiveness for myself and you. This is how Abd bin Hamid narrated it on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Dahhak on the authority of Mukhallad on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah with it. Another Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “Your lineage is not a source of insult to anyone. You are all the children of Adam, a small measure which they could not fill. No one has any superiority over anyone except through religion and piety. It is sufficient for a man to be vulgar, miserly, and obscene.” Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, with this wording: “People are like Adam and Eve, a small measure which they could not fill. God will not ask you about your lineage or ancestry on the Day of Resurrection. The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you.” It is not found in any of the Six Books from this source. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umaira, the husband of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, on the authority of Dhura bint Abi Lahab, may God be pleased with her, who said: A man stood up to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit and said: O Messenger of God, who are the best people? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best people are those who recite the Qur’an the most, who fear God Almighty the most, who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and who maintain kinship ties. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Abu Al-Aswad told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim Ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: Nothing in this world pleased the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one ever pleased him except the pious. Ahmad alone transmitted it. God the Almighty says: Indeed, God is All-Knowing and All-Aware. That is, He is All-Knowing and All-Aware of your affairs. He guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills, He has mercy on whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and He favors whom He wills over whom He wills. He is the Wise, All-Knowing, All-Aware in all of this. This noble verse and these noble hadiths were used as evidence by those scholars who held that compatibility in marriage is not a condition, and that only religion is a condition, based on the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. Others cited evidence mentioned in the books of jurisprudence, and we have mentioned some of that in The Book of Rulings, praise and thanks be to God. Al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman that he heard a man from Banu Hashim say: I am the closest of people to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and someone else said: I am more worthy of him than you and I have a relationship with him.
49:14: God the Almighty says, denouncing the Bedouins who, when they first entered Islam, claimed for themselves the status of faith, but faith had not yet taken root in their hearts: The desert Arabs say, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], ‘We have submitted,’ for faith has not yet entered your hearts. 49:18: God the Almighty says, denouncing the Bedouins who, when they first entered Islam, claimed for themselves the status of faith, but faith had not yet taken root in their hearts: The desert Arabs say, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], ‘We have submitted,’ for faith has not yet entered your hearts. [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] It has been understood from this noble verse that faith is more specific than Islam, as is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama’ah, and this is indicated by the hadith of Gabriel, peace be upon him, when he asked about Islam, then about faith, then about ihsan, so he progressed from the more general to the more specific, then to the more specific than it. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, from al-Zuhri, from Amir ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, gave to some men and did not give anything to one of them. Sa’d, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, you gave to so-and-so and so-and-so, but did not give anything to so-and-so, and he is a believer. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Or a Muslim? Until Sa'd may God be pleased with him repeated it three times, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Or a Muslim? Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I give to some men and leave out those who are dearer to me, so I did not give them anything for fear that they would fall on their faces into the Fire. [Bukhari and Muslim] Both of them reported it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Az-Zuhri. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) differentiated between the believer and the Muslim, which indicates that faith is more specific than Islam. We have established this with its evidence at the beginning of the explanation of the Book of Faith in Sahih Al-Bukhari, all praise and thanks be to God. This indicates that the man was a Muslim, not a hypocrite, because he left him the gift and left him to what he was in of Islam. This indicates that these Bedouins mentioned in this verse are not hypocrites, but rather they are Muslims whose faith was not firmly established in their hearts, so they claimed for themselves a higher status than what they had reached, so they were disciplined for that. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him, Ibrahim An-Nakha'i, and Qatadah, and it was chosen by Ibn Jarir. We said this because Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, believed that these people were hypocrites who pretended to have faith but were not. It was narrated on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and Ibn Zayd that they said about the words of God the Most High: But say, 'We have submitted,' meaning, we have surrendered for fear of being killed or taken captive. Mujahid said: It was revealed about Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah. Qatadah said: It was revealed about a people who boasted to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about their faith. The first and most correct version is that they were people who claimed to have the status of faith, but had not yet attained it. So they were disciplined and made aware that they had not yet attained it. Had they been hypocrites, they would have been reprimanded and disgraced, as the hypocrites were mentioned in Surah Bara'ah. Rather, it was said to these people as a form of discipline: Say, 'You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts, meaning you have not yet attained the true meaning of faith. Then God the Almighty said: {And if you obey God and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds} meaning, He will not diminish your rewards in the least, as God the Almighty said: {And We have not deprived them of anything of their deeds} and His saying: {Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful} meaning to whoever repents to Him and returns [to Him]. And His saying: {The believers} meaning, the perfect believers are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger and then have not doubted} meaning, they have not doubted or wavered, but rather they have remained steadfast in one state, which is pure belief, {and have striven with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God} meaning, they have sacrificed their lives and the most precious things in the obedience of God and seeking His pleasure. {Those are the truthful} meaning in what they say when they say that they are believers, not like some of the Bedouins who have nothing of faith except the outward word. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ghailan told us, Rashdin told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Samh, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The believers in this world are divided into three categories: those who believed in God and His Messenger, then did not doubt and fought with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, and those whom people trust with their wealth and their lives, and those who, when they are on the verge of greed, leave it for God Almighty.” And the words of God Almighty: Say, ‘Do you inform God of your religion?’ That is, do you inform Him of what is in your hearts? And God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? That is, not an atom’s weight on the earth or in the heavens is hidden from Him, nor anything smaller or larger than that. And God is Knowing of all things. Then God Almighty said: “They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. Say, ‘Do not bestow upon me your Islam.’” That is, the Bedouins who do you a favor by becoming Muslims, following and supporting the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty says in response to them: Say, ‘Do not bestow upon me a favor.’ Your Islam.” The benefit of that will only come back to you, and God has bestowed favor upon you in it. Rather, God has bestowed favor upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you should be truthful, that is, in your claim to that, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Ansar on the day of Hunayn: O group of Ansar, did I not find you astray and God guided you through me? And you were divided and God united you through me? And you were poor and God enriched you through me? Every time he said something, they said: God and His Messenger believe. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ibrahim bin Saeed al-Jawhari narrated to us, Yahya bin Saeed al-Umawi narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais, on the authority of Abu Awn, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Banu Asad came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we have become Muslims and the Arabs fought you, but we did not fight you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Their understanding is little, and Satan speaks through their tongues. Then this verse was revealed: “They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. Say: ‘Do not do me a favor by your Islam. Rather, God has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you should be truthful.’” Then he said: We do not know of it being narrated except through this source, and we do not know that Abu Awn Muhammad bin Ubaidullah narrated from Saeed bin Jubair other than this hadith. Then he repeated the statement of His knowledge of all beings and His vision of the deeds of His creatures, saying: “Indeed, God knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And God is Seeing of what you do.” (The end of the interpretation of Surat al-Hujurat. To God be praise and thanks, and to Him belongs success and protection.
